title: The watched atom (quantum Zeno effect)

data.source: Monte Carlo of repeated ideal measurements on a driven two-level system, standard quantum rule, seeded

prediction: The flip comes when the turning added up between looks reaches half a turn, however often anyone looks: the summed count at the flip stays within 10 % of one half turn for 1 to 32 looks.
baseline: Standard quantum mechanics: a look that finds no flip puts the state back to the start, so the summed count at the flip grows like 4n/pi half turns for n looks.
why: The count at the flip is not fixed. It grows with the number of looks exactly as quantum mechanics says, because each look empties the count. CRR has no rule for that unless it borrows the quantum one.
